summary: Configured daily logrotate for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 with 7 kept compressed rotations using copytruncate (so the writer keeps its file descriptor and can continue writing after rotation), verified functionally, then restarted node1 per protocol and re-verified everything survived.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: confirmed logrotate-3.22.0-4.el10 installed, systemd logrotate.timer runs daily, /var/log/inventory/app.log exists with no active writer process (static seeded content)
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with: daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Forced a rotation (logrotate -f) and confirmed: app.log kept the same inode (copytruncate preserved the file), app.log.1.gz created and compressed, original content preserved in the rotated file
Wrote to app.log after rotation to prove the application can keep writing without restart/reopen
Ran 8 additional forced rotation cycles to prove only 7 rotations (app.log.1.gz..app.log.7.gz) are retained, with older ones pruned
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, logrotate.timer active/enabled state, directory listing, and config contents
Rebooted node1 via 'sudo -n systemctl reboot', acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified boot_id changed and uptime reset, confirming an actual restart occurred
Post-restart: verified logrotate.timer active/enabled, logrotate.d config persisted, all rotated log files persisted

Post-restart functional re-check: wrote a new log entry, forced another rotation (same inode preserved again), then wrote again after rotation to reconfirm continued-writing behavior survives the reboot

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with 7 kept compressed rotations configured for /var/log/inventory/app.log
evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app (daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate), validated syntax, then ran 8 forced rotation cycles showing exactly app.log.1.gz through app.log.7.gz retained (older pruned) and each rotated file gzip-compressed

evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing to app.log after rotation
evidence.summary: copytruncate confirmed: app.log inode 290760 identical before (baseline) and after forced rotation (size 60 -> 0, same inode); a write immediately after rotation succeeded and appeared in app.log
Captured boot_id 368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a, logrotate.timer active+enabled, and healthy log directory/config state prior to restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: sudo systemctl reboot was dispatched and acknowledged; exec stream closed as the node went down, consistent with a real reboot in progress

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Connection timed out / reset while node1 was down, then exec succeeded again; boot_id changed to 7a0135bc-03a6-48c6-aedf-8acbeda106e1 (differs from baseline) and uptime -s reset to the restart time, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required service/config/data and continued rotation+writability
evidence.summary: After reboot: logrotate.timer active/enabled, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app config intact, all 7 rotated .gz files intact; a new write, a forced rotation (inode preserved again), and a post-rotation write all succeeded, confirming full functional recovery
